newsitem.title: SPAIN: Three gunmen storm Italian consulate in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Three gunmen storm Italian consulate in Spain.

text.p: Three armed men stormed an office housing the Italian consulate in Malaga on Wednesday, tied up the employees and forced them to read a statement, an Italian embassy spokesman in Madrid said.

"Three men entered and immobilised the employees and made them read a statement written in Spanish which said...it was an action by a revolutionary group to protest against Italian justice and in favour of prisoners," the spokesman told Reuters.

The embassy said it did not know the identities of the men, who carried pistols as they forced their way into the consular department in the southern Spanish resort, or anything about the prisoners to whom they referred.
The embassy said Italy's honorary vice-consul Juan Jimenez Aguilar was not present when the office was stormed and that two employees were seized hostage and tied up with tape.
The embassy spokesman said the gunmen may have been referring to recent incidents along Spain's Costa del Sol southern coast, Spanish news agencies said.
The statement, which one of the consulate employees was forced to read, said that such attacks would be repeated in all countries where the justice system worked like that of Italy.
The men, aged 25-30, wore black trousers and jackets and spoke good Spanish.

They spray-painted the walls of the consulate office, which is used for processing documents and lacks security, and stole some passports, official stamps and money, which made the Italian embassy wonder about the motives for the attack.
"The impression we have is that it was done by common delinquents who tried to cover up their activities," the embassy spokesman said of the men, who disappeared without trace.
